subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a unit of electric potential?
solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Newton per Coulomb**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Newton per Coulomb is a unit of electric field, **not electric potential**.
 
• The electric **field is defined as the force experienced by a unit positive charge due to an electric charge at a particular distance**.
 
• It is measured in** Newton per Coulomb (N/C)**.
 
• **Electric field (E) at a point** is defined as the force experienced by a positive test charge (q₀) placed at that point: E = (F)/(q₀) 
 
• where:
 
 
• **(E) is the electric field strength in newtons per coulomb (N/C).**
 
• **(F) is the force experienced by the test charge.**
 
• **(q₀) is the magnitude of the test charge.**
 
 
 
• **Electric potential, on the other hand, is related to energy, not force**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Volt (V):**

 
 
• The **volt is the standard unit of electric potential difference or voltage.**
 
• It represents the amount of potential energy per unit charge.
 
• Mathematically, electric potential difference ((V)) between two points is given by: V = (W)/(q) , where:
 
• **(V) is the potential difference (voltage) in volts.**
 
• **(W) is the work done (energy) in joules.**
 
• **(q) is the charge in coulombs.**
 
• For example,** if a battery provides a potential difference of 9 volts, it means that each coulomb of charge gains 9 joules of energy when moving from the negative terminal to the positive terminal of the battery.**
 
 
 
• **Newton-Meter per Coulomb (N·m/C):**
 
 
• A Newton meter is a unit of work, which is energy transferred.
 
• **Since energy per charge (work done per unit charge) is the definition of electric potential, so Newton-meter per Coulomb is a unit of electric potential.**
 
 
 
• **Joules per Coulomb (J/C):**
 
 
• This unit is **equivalent to the volt (V).**
 
• Electric potential can be expressed in joules per coulomb or volts.
 
• The relationship between potential energy (U) and potential difference (V) is: **U = qV **where:
 
• **(U) is the potential energy in joules.**
 
• **(q) is the charge in coulombs.**
 
• **(V) is the potential difference in volts.**
